prompts.name: flora-v4
prompts.prompt: Create a production-ready PIXEL ART sprite atlas of SIX different isolated alpine roadside plants. Reference image is style reference only. Transparent background with real alpha. Strict 3 columns by 2 rows, large empty separation, each entire object fully contained within its cell. Top row: fern clump with layered feathered fronds, cluster of tiny white wildflowers and rounded olive leaves, a low sprawling dark juniper shrub. Bottom row: young slender birch tree with white bark and sparse olive canopy, dead broken stump with moss and small roots, clump of purple alpine flowers mixed with straw-colored blades. Painted crisp stepped pixel clusters matching vegetation in reference, irregular natural silhouettes and dense overlapping leaves, dark olive shadows warm sunset edge light, no blurry gradients no outlines no cartoon neon. Whole objects front/three-quarter view for vertical game billboards. No ground slab, no detached shadows, no rocks or background scenery, no text. Four plants must differ clearly from grass and pine trees. Each cell has complete plant with empty margins, base near cell bottom.

Crisp hand-painted pixel clusters matching reference character, fine detailed cloth folds, hard pixel edges, consistent sunset lighting. Distinct readable silhouettes. Wide sprite atlas.

prompts.name: panorama-east

Use fine crisp painted PIXEL ART at 1-2 pixel detail scale like the reference, many tiny rocks and roof details, no coarse pixel enlargement, no photorealism or blurry gradients. This must harmonize with the reference when shown in a game camera rotating into the next direction.

prompts.name: panorama-full
prompts.prompt: Create ONE CONTINUOUS 360-degree CYLINDRICAL PANORAMA for the distant environment of an alpine downhill pixel-art game. Output an ultra-wide panoramic strip 3840 by 1280 pixels (3:1 aspect ratio). Use supplied image only as style/color reference, not as a framing constraint. The panorama must show a single coherent connected Alpine landscape across the entire width: forested mountain valleys, violet snowy ranges, a connected blue lake in one portion, a winding river and tiny hamlets elsewhere. Camera stands high above a Swiss valley. Pink orange sunset sky, exactly one small pale yellow sun located about one quarter from left. Sky occupies upper 35 percent, mountain skyline near 35-45 percent height, distant valley terrain and lake lower half. Left and right edges must join seamlessly into each other in sky color, cloud lines and forested hills (no sun or major peak near seam). Very broad vista, not a normal camera view stretched wider. No panel divisions, no montage, no separate views, no foreground road, trees close to camera, railings, person or text. High-end painted PIXEL ART using tiny 1-2 pixel clusters at this large native resolution, finely detailed cliff strata, roofs and treetops, subtle atmospheric blue haze separating ridges, no giant pixel blocks, no blur or photorealism. Keep relief gently varied and open so mountains fit within the frame rather than being cut off. Continuity across the strip matters more than copying any exact mountain from reference.

notes: Generated using image_gen. Original PNG pixels/alpha preserved; runtime assets serialized losslessly. valley-v2, panorama-east and panorama-west are intermediate explorations and are not loaded in the final runtime. The final panorama is actually 2172x724, not the requested 3840x1280.
